title: Adjusting to Working from Home
paragraphs: When his company shifts to allowing remote work twice a week, Ferdi struggles at first to separate his work hours from his personal time while sitting at the same kitchen table all day.
During the first few weeks, he finds himself checking messages late into the evening, unable to mentally close his workday the way he naturally could when he physically left an office building.
His wife suggests setting a clear routine instead, including changing clothes each morning and closing his laptop at a fixed time every evening, treating it like a real commute even without one.
After adopting this small routine, Ferdi notices his evenings feel calmer and more present with his family, realizing that structure, not just location, was what actually made work feel like work.
